title: Cordoba takes oath as new SC justice
summary: Former Commission on Audit chairman Gamaliel Cordoba has been admitted to the Supreme Court (SC) as its newest associate justice.

blocks.text: Former Commission on Audit (COA) chairman Gamaliel Cordoba
MANILA, Philippines — Former Commission on Audit (COA) chairman Gamaliel Cordoba has been admitted to the Supreme Court (SC) as its newest associate justice.
Cordoba took his oath of office before Chief Justice Rodil Zalameda at the SC session hall yesterday.

Members of Cordoba’s family, Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen, SC Associate Justices Ricardo Rosario, Jhosep Lopez, Antonio Kho Jr. and Raul Villanueva, and former chief justice Alexander Gesmundo witnessed his swearing in.

Cordoba will be the 196th associate justice of the high court and the third person to be appointed by President Marcos following Villanueva as associate justice in June 2025 and Zalameda as chief justice on Nov. 5.
Cordoba will replace former SC associate justice Amy Lazaro-Javier, who retired on her 70th birthday on Nov. 16.
He will be the 14th member of the 15-man bench, with the position of SC associate justice vacated by Zalameda still open for application until Dec. 28.

According to Malacañang, the COA under Cordoba filed “at least 50 audit reports” related to flood control projects before the Office of the Ombudsman and the defunct Independent Commission for Infrastructure and required GPS-based geotagging of all government infrastructure projects as part of compliance to verification measures.

In a public interview by the Judicial and Bar Council last month, Cordoba vowed to support the SC’s Strategic Plan for Judicial Innovations 2022-2027 and said he may introduce more improvements, such as using satellite internet to make court processes more accessible, digitalizing court procedures to avoid corrupt practices in face-to-face interactions and issuing decisions in Filipino.
